text: I Am... Sasha Fierce is the third studio album by American singer and songwriter Beyoncé, released on November 12, 2008, by Columbia Records and Music World Entertainment. The album was recorded from November 2007 to August 2008 over a nine-month period, with production handled by Darkchild, Toby Gad, Jim Jonsin, Rico Love, Stargate, Tricky Stewart, Ryan Tedder of OneRepublic, and The-Dream, alongside others. Although there are no featured artists on the main track listing, Lady Gaga and Kanye West appear on the deluxe editions. The album is formatted as a double album, reflecting Beyoncé's dual artistic personas: the first disc, I Am..., features slow and midtempo pop and R&B ballads, while the second, Sasha Fierce—named after her on-stage alter ego—focuses on uptempo electropop and Europop tracks. Beyoncé co-wrote or co-produced all material on the album and worked with producers and songwriters including Babyface, Stargate, Tricky Stewart, The-Dream, Darkchild, Sean Garrett, Solange Knowles, Jim Jonsin, Rico Love, Ryan Tedder, Bangladesh, Ian Dench, Dave McCracken, Wayne Wilkins, and Blac Elvis. She also collaborated with Toby Gad and BC Jean on "If I Were a Boy" and worked again with Amanda Ghost on "Disappear." Beyoncé credited her husband Jay-Z and jazz singer Etta James for inspiring her songwriting. Musically, the I Am... disc draws from folk and alternative rock, incorporating acoustic guitar, while Sasha Fierce features electronic influences, with songs like "Radio" and "Sweet Dreams" showcasing those elements. The ballads were crafted to blend pop and soul, expanding both genres, and Beyoncé experimented with stronger lyrics to break from expectations. "Ave Maria" samples Franz Schubert's "Ave Maria" after being co-written with Ghost, who noted they were inspired by their recent marriages. "Smash Into You," originally intended for Jon McLaughlin's album, was given to Beyoncé after being leaked. During the recording process, Beyoncé recorded over seventy songs and eliminated those that were meaningless to her, resulting in twelve tracks on the standard edition and five additional tracks on the deluxe edition. Songs from producers like The Neptunes and Danja were not included. The album received mixed to positive reviews and was a commercial success, debuting at number one on the US Billboard 200 with first-week sales of 482,000 units, earning Beyoncé her third consecutive US number-one solo album. It has earned one diamond and over thirty platinum certifications worldwide, achieving seven-times platinum status by the RIAA after shipping over seven million units in the United States and selling 10 million copies globally, making it one of the best-selling albums of the 21st century. The album received seven Grammy nominations at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards (2010), including Album of the Year, winning five, with a sixth win during the ceremony, making Beyoncé the female artist with the most awards won in one night. Singles such as "If I Were a Boy" and "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)" charted highly internationally, with the former topping charts in over ten countries and reaching number three on the Billboard Hot 100, and the latter becoming her fifth number-one single on the Hot 100. "Diva" and "Ego" were released exclusively in the United States, while "Halo" and "Sweet Dreams" were promoted internationally as the third and fourth singles, respectively. "Broken-Hearted Girl" was released internationally as the fifth single, and "Video Phone" was released in September 2009 as the eighth single, with "Why Don't You Love Me" released in July 2010 as the ninth and final single. The album was marketed with televised appearances and award show performances across Europe and America, and Beyoncé embarked on the worldwide I Am... Tour (2009–10). The recording took place at studios in Atlanta, New York, Ibiza, Los Angeles, Miami Beach, and Burbank. The I Am... cover, described as "underneath all the makeup," shows Beyoncé without clothing or makeup, while the Sasha Fierce cover features heavy makeup, a leotard, tall heels, and a "cyborg"-esque metallic glove, both shot by Peter Lindbergh. Beyoncé revealed in a 2021 Harper's Bazaar interview that she based the project on black and white photography after being upset by a fan survey suggesting her fans disliked black and white images, highlighting her frustration with corporate formulas and noting the album's commercial success. The album was released in the United States on November 18, 2008, previously in Japan on November 12, Australia and Germany on November 14, and France and the United Kingdom on November 17; the deluxe edition was released simultaneously. Beyoncé promoted the album through performances on shows including Music Station, the MTV Europe Music Awards, the World Music Awards, The Oprah Winfrey Show, Saturday Night Live, and various others, with her first live performance of "Halo" at the 40th NAACP Image Awards in February 2009 and a performance of "Sweet Dreams" at the 2009 MTV Europe Music Awards in November 2009. She performed "If I Were a Boy" at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards in January 2010, along with a cover of Alanis Morissette's "You Oughta Know." The bonus track "Why Don't You Love Me" reached number one on the US Dance Club Songs chart in February 2010. A music video for the full-length track was released online on May 4, 2010. On June 16, 2009, Above and Beyoncé: Video Collection & Dance Mixes was released, including a remix of "Ego" with Kanye West and behind-the-scenes footage. Beyoncé was scheduled to perform "Sweet Dreams" at the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards but only performed the bridge before switching to "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)." The platinum edition was released in Australia on September 4, 2009, and in the United States on October 20, 2009, including a cover of Billy Joel's "Honesty" and a DVD of music videos. The deluxe edition was reissued in the United States on November 23, 2009, with new tracks "Poison" and the remix of "Video Phone" with Lady Gaga, and an EP titled I Am... Sasha Fierce – The Bonus Tracks was released the same day for digital download, featuring those songs and "Why Don't You Love Me." The album formally introduces Sasha Fierce, who Beyoncé revealed was born during the making of "Crazy in Love" (2003), and described as her sensual, aggressive stage alter ego. In an interview with Emmet Sullivan, Beyoncé affirmed that Sasha Fierce is strictly for the stage. The I Am... disc was described by Beyoncé as having mainstream songs and traditional R&B for her long-time fans, with influences from Barbra Streisand, Karen Carpenter, and The Beatles from the 1970s. Music writer Andy Kellman noted the first disc as a set of adult contemporary ballads with roots in 1970s soft rock, while the second disc features consistent electronic elements. "Diva" was noted as a variation on Lil Wayne's "A Milli," and "Sweet Dreams" was praised for its electronic bassline, compared to Michael Jackson's "Beat It," and derived from contemporary R&B with 1980s funk influences. "Broken-Hearted Girl" is a midtempo piano ballad with strings and a drum machine beat. "Hello" includes the line "You had me at hello" and features sweet guitar-picking and delicate harmonies. "Video Phone" contains lyrics referencing Skype sex and a solo performance for a new acquaintance, with a remixed version featuring Beyoncé and Lady Gaga trading verses and gasps and groans. "Disappear" features sweet guitar-picking and delicate harmonies. "That's Why You're Beautiful" is a slow-tempo soft rock and rock power ballad with a grungy guitar riff and stuttering drums, compared to Alice in Chains and Jill Scott. The platinum edition includes a cover of Billy Joel's "Honesty" (1979). The album was titled I Am... Sasha Fierce to highlight the contrast between Beyoncé and her alter ego.

The platinum edition of I Am... Sasha Fierce was released in Australia on Beyoncé's twenty-eighth birthday, September 4, 2009, and in the United States on October 20, 2009; it included a cover version of Billy Joel's "Honesty" (1979) and a DVD with music videos from the album's singles. The deluxe edition was reissued in the United States on November 23, 2009, containing all previously released songs plus new tracks "Poison" and the remix of "Video Phone" with Lady Gaga. On the same day, an EP titled I Am... Sasha Fierce – The Bonus Tracks was released digitally in the United States, featuring "Poison," the "Video Phone" remix, and "Why Don't You Love Me." To promote the album, Beyoncé launched the I Am... Tour, beginning in Edmonton, Canada on March 26, 2009, with the European leg starting April 26 in Zagreb, Croatia, and ending June 9 in London, England. The third leg began June 21 in the United States and concluded in August with the I Am... Yours four-day residency at Encore Las Vegas on the Las Vegas Strip. The fourth leg started September 15 in Melbourne, Australia and ended September 24 in Perth, Australia, followed by performances in Asia, the Middle East, Europe, Africa, and the United Kingdom, finishing on November 24 in Belfast, Northern Ireland. The final leg in February 2010 began in Florianópolis, Brazil and ended in Trinidad on February 18. According to Pollstar, the 2010 shows earned $17.2 million, adding to the $86 million from the first 86 concerts in 2009, bringing the tour total to $103.2 million for 97 shows. The I Am... Yours residency at Encore Theater was recorded on August 2, 2009, and released as a DVD, audio CD, and television special titled I Am... Yours: An Intimate Performance at Wynn Las Vegas in late November 2009. Various tour performances were filmed worldwide for the live DVD I Am... World Tour, released on November 30, 2010. On October 8, 2008, Beyoncé premiered two lead singles, "If I Were a Boy," which peaked at number three on the US Billboard Hot 100, topped eight charts worldwide, and reached the top ten on many others, and "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)," which peaked at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Beyoncé's fifth number-one single and reaching the top ten globally. Both singles were certified double platinum and quadruple platinum, respectively, by the RIAA. "Diva," released exclusively in the United States, peaked at number nineteen on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Beyoncé's twelfth top-twenty single and number three on the US Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs, and was certified gold by the RIAA. "Halo," released internationally, peaked at number five on the US Billboard Hot 100 and reached the top ten worldwide, certified double platinum by the RIAA on January 5, 2010. Two additional singles, "Broken-Hearted Girl" and "Sweet Dreams," were initially announced but became the sixth and seventh singles, respectively. "Sweet Dreams" reached the top ten in most countries, including the United States, topped the New Zealand Singles Chart, and was certified platinum by the RIAA on January 5, 2010. "Broken-Hearted Girl," the seventh single, reached the top forty globally without certification or release in the United States. "Video Phone," released as the eighth single on September 22, 2009, with a music video and digital download, featured a remix with Lady Gaga, reached the top forty worldwide, peaked at number sixty-five on the US Billboard Hot 100, and became Beyoncé's fourteenth number-one on the US Hot Dance Club Songs. "Why Don't You Love Me" was released as the ninth and final single on July 2, 2010, and peaked atop the US Hot Dance Club Songs before its official release. As of July 2010, digital tracks from the album had sold 12.3 million units in the United States, and according to Columbia Records, the album had sold fifteen million digital singles worldwide. I Am... Sasha Fierce received mixed reviews; at Metacritic, it received an average score of 62 based on 24 reviews, indicating generally favorable reviews. Sal Cinquemani of Slant Magazine praised the individual songs as a testament to Beyoncé's reliability as a singles artist but criticized the album's inability to reconcile the adult-contemporary style of "I Am" with the edgier sounds of "Sasha Fierce." Adam Mattera of The Observer found both discs lacking depth, criticizing the first for chasing radio formats and the second for its "independent woman anthems" that appeal to drag queens but confuse others. AllMusic's Andy Kellman called the double-disc "gimmick" flimsy, favoring the second disc's upbeat pop, noting that Beyoncé's vocal performance on the "I Am" disc almost rescues its staidness. Robert Christgau of MSN Music named it the "dud of the month," calling it a bad record with few details worth considering and criticizing its "split-personality" as "deeply vapid," noting only three good songs. Jonah Weiner of Blender described Beyoncé as a "beauty-shop feminist" with poise in describing love. Stacey Anderson of Spin noted the first disc meanders over down-tempo cuts and called "Sasha" an intriguing but diluted direction. Nana Ekua Brew-Hammond of The Village Voice found the "I Am" disc lacking cohesion but praised "Sasha Fierce" as "brassy, big-headed, confrontational, and witty," stating each track challenges the listener to leave inhibitions at the door. Christian Hoard of Rolling Stone noted the slow songs are full of bland self-affirmation but praised the "Sasha" disc as Beyoncé's most adventurous music yet. Colin McGuire of PopMatters called the album a little rough around the edges and viewed the "Sasha" disc as a more compelling dance-oriented experience. Leah Greenblatt of Entertainment Weekly stated the album offers two compelling sides of Beyoncé and suggested it might have been better as a single disc, noting that the lyrics offer little new emotional insight. Sasha Frere-Jones of The New Yorker found the album a "mess" due to the alter ego tripping on the idea of redefinition. Greenblatt ranked I Am... Sasha Fierce at number two on her list "10 Best CDs of 2008," highlighting "If I Were a Boy" and "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)" as highlights and noting the rest of the album is consistently satisfying on repeated listening. Mark Edward Nero of About.com ranked it ninth on his list of the Best R&B Albums of 2008. Christian Gerard of NBC Washington included it in his "Honorable Mentions" list for "Best Albums of 2008." Agence France-Presse, as reported by ABS-CBN News and Current Affairs, recognized it as the twelfth best-selling album of 2008. On The Village Voice's Pazz & Jop year-end lists, it was ranked 333rd in 2008 and 580th in 2009. It was ranked number twelve on Rolling Stone's Reader's Poll for the best albums of the 2000s decade and number eight on Entertainment Weekly's list of the "10 Best Albums of the Decade." The album won a Soul Train Music Award for Best Album of the Year at the 2009 Soul Train Music Awards. Beyoncé won the American Music Award for Favorite Soul/R&B Female Artist at the 2009 American Music Awards, with I Am... Sasha Fierce receiving a nomination for Favorite Soul/R&B Album. Beyoncé also won a BET Award for Best R&B Artist at the 2009 BET Awards, though she lost the same award to Alicia Keys at the following ceremony. She was nominated for the Brit Award for International Female Solo Artist at the 2009 Brit Awards, the Meteor Music Award for Best International Female at the 2009 Meteor Awards, and the International Dance Music Awards for Best Artist (Solo) and Best R&B/Urban Dance Track for "Sweet Dreams" at the 25th Annual International Dance Music Awards in 2010. At the MOBO Awards 2009, Beyoncé won the MOBO Award for Best International Act and I Am... Sasha Fierce was nominated for Best Album. Beyoncé won an MTV Europe Music Award for Best Female, "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)" won Best Video, and "Halo" won Best Song at the 2009 MTV Europe Music Awards. The album was nominated for the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Album at the 40th NAACP Image Awards in 2009 and for an NRJ Music Award for International Album of the Year at the NRJ Music Awards 2010. Beyoncé was nominated for a People's Choice Award for Favorite Female Artist and Favorite R&B Artist at the 36th People's Choice Awards in 2010, won a Teen Choice Award for Choice Music: R&B Artist at the 2010 Teen Choice Awards, and was nominated for World's Best R&B Artist at the 2010 World Music Awards. I Am... Sasha Fierce and its singles earned Beyoncé seven Grammy Award nominations at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards in 2010, including Album of the Year; she won five, and also won a record-breaking sixth for her rendition of "At Last" from the Cadillac Records soundtrack, making her the most decorated female artist in one night in Grammy history. The album debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200, selling 482,000 copies in its first week and giving Beyoncé her third consecutive number-one album in the United States, her fourth overall, including Destiny's Child's Survivor (2001). This made her the third female artist of the 2000s to have her first three solo albums debut at number one. By the end of 2008, the album had sold 1,459,000 copies in six weeks and became the tenth best-selling album of the year according to Billboard. This achievement placed Beyoncé in a tie with Garth Brooks, Mariah Carey, and Shania Twain for having an album in Nielsen SoundScan's year-end top ten for the fifth time. The album became the second best-selling album of 2009 in the United States and was certified six-times platinum by the RIAA. As of July 2022, it has sold 8.12 million album-equivalent units in the United States. In the United Kingdom, it debuted at number ten on November 29, 2008, becoming Beyoncé's lowest-debuting album despite higher first-week sales than B'Day (2006), rose to number nine after a performance with Alexandra Burke on The X Factor fifth season finale on December 27, 2008, and reached its highest peak of number two in its thirty-ninth week on August 16, 2009, due to the success of singles like "Sweet Dreams," making it her best-selling album in the UK with over 1.5 million units sold and certified six times platinum by the British Phonographic Industry. In Australia, it debuted at number nine on November 24, 2008, climbed to number eight on January 5, 2009, and reached number three on two separate occasions in October 2009 following the success of "Sweet Dreams" and "Broken-Hearted Girl," later certified quintuple platinum by the ARIA in 2023. In New Zealand, it debuted at number sixteen on November 24, 2008, peaked at number six on March 2, 2009, and reached number three on September 21, 2009, after the success of "Sweet Dreams," certified platinum by RIANZ after twenty-three weeks on the chart with over 15,000 copies shipped. In Spain, it debuted and peaked at number seven on November 26, 2008, and was certified double platinum by PROMUSICAE for over 160,000 copies. The album was the best-selling international album of 2009 in Turkey. It topped Brazil's year-end chart and was certified double diamond for sales over 500,000 copies by Pro-Música Brasil. The album has sold over ten million copies worldwide and generated over 1 billion streams as of February 2017.
The figures provided are based solely on certification, not including sales and streaming data. Sales and streaming figures are also based only on certification.
